observation.what_happens: A blue block hanging from a vertical spring oscillates up and down above a striped bar. It starts released from a low stretched position, bounces up and down with decreasing amplitude until it rests at equilibrium.

reasoning: The s data shows ~0.6 s period vertical oscillation about ~100 px with slowly shrinking amplitude from ~90 px, typical of a lightly damped spring-mass. Candidates go from textbook undamped to linear viscous damping in air to viscous plus quadratic air drag for high-speed losses.

Dry friction treated as constant while moving, ignoring sticking at rest
critique.finding: The block bounces on its spring with natural wobble {w0} around rest spot {s_eq}. It slows from light air drag {gamma} plus steady dry rubbing {ac}.
critique.headline: The spring block slows from rubbing as well as air.
critique.why_it_won: It adds constant dry rubbing to viscous drag, so it follows the steady shrinking of the swings that viscous-only laws leave as large waves.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that always pushes opposite the motion on top of viscous damping. The misses swing with the oscillation instead of looking like noise, showing the pure exponential envelope gets the decay shape slightly wrong.

headline: The spring block slows from rubbing as well as air.
finding: The block bounces on its spring with natural wobble 10.0007 ± 0.0019 rad/s around rest spot 98.142 ± 0.067 pixel. It slows from light air drag 0.030 ± 0.038 1/s plus steady dry rubbing 355 ± 23 pixel/s².

eyeball.confidence: low - single thumbnail only, timing estimated from typical damped oscillation
eyeball.law_in_words: Vertical spring-mass is a viscously damped harmonic oscillator about equilibrium: acceleration = -w0^2*(x - s_eq) - gamma*velocity.

wonder.idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that always pushes opposite the motion on top of viscous damping. The misses swing with the oscillation instead of looking like noise, showing the pure exponential envelope gets the decay shape slightly wrong.

Extending the friction model with a sign-based Coulomb term and smoothing, and setting parameter bounds for fitting.
